query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Employing a hybrid approach that combines the TOR-TILD method with machine learning potentials (MLPs) can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in the solid state
generation.intervention: Hybrid TOR-TILD and MLP approach with a training set of ab initio molecular dynamics simulations
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 500-2000 K, Composition range: 3-6 principal elements
generation.mechanism: The hybrid approach leverages the accuracy of TOR-TILD for elemental and binary systems and the efficiency of MLPs for multicomponent systems, allowing for the retention of vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling
generation.predicted_outcome: A 5-10 fold reduction in computational cost relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and a 2-5 fold reduction relative to TOR-TILD, with a fidelity of 90-95% in predicting phase free energies and derived observables
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the hybrid approach may depend on the quality of the training set and the complexity of the multicomponent system

falsification_experiment.design: Compute phase free energies and derived observables for a set of multicomponent high-entropy alloys using the hybrid TOR-TILD and MLP approach and compare with explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows
measurements: Derived observables such as entropy and heat capacity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the mean absolute error (MAE) between the hybrid approach and explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows exceeds 10% for phase free energies and derived observables, the hypothesis is falsified
